questions.questionText: hour Additional Materials: Multiple Choice Answer Sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) READ THESE INSTRUCTIONS FIRST Write in soft pencil. Do not use staples, paper clips, glue or correction fluid. Write your name, Centre number and candidate number on the Answer Sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. DO NOT WRITE IN ANY BARCODES. There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any rough working should be done in this booklet.

A firm is considering whether to buy a piece of capital equipment which will cost $2000. It estimates that the equipment will last for two years. The alternative is to lend the money to a finance company at a compound rate of interest of 5%. What is the minimum increase in revenue the firm must expect to make it worthwhile buying the equipment?

The diagram shows the production possibility curve XX of an economy that produces both consumer goods and capital goods. X M capital N goods X O consumer goods If the economy moves from point M to point N, which diagram represents the most likely position of the production possibility curve YY in the future?

options.A: B X X Y Y capital capital goods goods Y X Y X O consumer goods O consumer goods
options.C: D X Y capital Y capital X goods goods X Y X Y O consumer goods O consumer goods

questions.questionText: Arfan and his brother Ben own and run a fishing business together. They have one boat and on the days when they fish they employ Cephas and Dipak. They sell the fish to the owner of a local shop. Which row correctly identifies the factors of production involved? land labour capital enterprise

options.A: shop Arfan and money paid shop owner Ben for the fish
options.B: shop Cephas and boat Arfan Dipak
options.C: the fish Ben money paid shop owner for the fish
options.D: the fish Cephas and boat Arfan and Dipak Ben

questions.questionText: The market price of a product rose from $8 to $10 and as a result the market demand fell from 20000 to 8000 a week. Consumer X’s demand declined from 30 to 24 and consumer Y’s demand fell from 100 to 60 a week. What can be concluded from this information?

options.A: Consumer X’s demand for the product was more elastic than the market demand.
options.B: Consumer X’s percentage share of the market increased.
options.C: Producer’s total profit fell.

questions.questionText: A government wishes to impose a tax on a good so that the producer and not the consumer pays most of the tax increase. Which level of price elasticity of demand would it be best for the good to have to achieve this aim?

options.A: price elasticity of demand is elastic
options.B: price elasticity of demand is inelastic
options.C: price elasticity of demand is perfectly inelastic
options.D: price elasticity of demand is unitary

questions.questionText: The demand for a commodity has unitary price elasticity. Which diagram shows the relationship between total expenditure on the commodity and its price?

options.A: B total total expenditure expenditure O O price price
options.C: D total total expenditure expenditure O O price price

questions.questionText: The price of good X rises by 10%. As a result, the demand for a substitute good Y rises by 20%. What is the cross-elasticity of demand for good Y with respect to the price of good X?
The diagram shows the supply curve of coffee in an economy. supply Y price X O quantity The market equilibrium is initially at point X, but a change moves it to point Y. What might explain this?

options.A: an increase in wages paid by producers of coffee
options.B: a switch in consumer tastes from coffee to tea
options.C: an increase in the price of tea
options.D: a tax imposed on coffee producers

questions.questionText: In the diagram OS and OS are two straight-line supply curves.
In which case will a given increase in the supply of a good cause the greatest fall in the price of the good?

options.A: when the demand for the good is perfectly inelastic
options.B: when the demand for the good is infinite
options.C: when the good is an inferior good
options.D: when the good’s price elasticity of demand is positive

questions.questionText: The table shows the maximum price a consumer would be willing to pay for successive cans of fruit juice. cans first second third fourth fifth price ($) 14 10 6 4 3 The price of a can of fruit juice is $4 and, having bought three cans, the consumer decides to buy a fourth. How does buying the fourth can affect his consumer surplus?

options.A: It leaves it unchanged.
options.C: It raises it by $4.

questions.questionText: Which combination of changes would enable the price mechanism to allocate resources more efficiently in a monopoly market? consumer producer sovereignty sovereignty

options.A: decrease decrease
options.C: increase decrease

questions.questionText: A firm wishes to build a factory extension. Permission is required from the government because the extension may increase

options.A: comparative costs.
options.C: opportunity costs.

25 quantity If there is no government intervention, what is the value of the marginal external benefit?
What can be provided only as a public good?

options.A: road use
options.C: street lighting

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the demand for and supply of a foreign-made mobile (cell) phone. The initial position in the domestic market is X. S E S F price G X D D O quantity Importers increased the supply of the phone and there was an increase in demand for the phone. The government considered whether to protect domestic manufacturers with a limit on imports which would keep the supply at the initial quantity. How would the price change between the new equilibrium without a limit on imports and the equilibrium with a limit on imports?

options.A: a movement from E to F
options.B: a movement from F to G
options.C: a movement from G to E
options.D: a movement from G to F

questions.questionText: The government imposes a maximum price of P on a product. S P P price D O Q Q Q
What is an effect on a country of free trade?

options.A: greater diversification of locally produced goods
options.B: greater efficiency in the resource use
options.C: greater independence in production

questions.questionText: As a result of a trade agreement, toys produced in Africa can be supplied to European markets. These toys are much cheaper than similar toys produced in Europe but are not of such good quality. What will happen in Europe to expenditure on toys, employment in European toy companies and imports from Africa? expenditure employment imports

options.A: decrease decrease decrease
options.C: increase uncertain increase

questions.questionText: Which international transaction is correctly matched to the part of the balance of payments account in which it is recorded? transaction part of account

options.A: the outflow of funds from national balancing item reserves to foreign residents
options.B: the provision of banking financial section services to foreign companies
options.C: the purchase of shares capital section in foreign banks
options.D: the receipt of interest on income section loans to foreign companies

questions.questionText: The diagram shows annual average labour productivity growth for three groups of countries during two time periods. 1975-1990 1990-2005 key agriculture Latin America East Asia high-income countries –1 1975-1990 1990-2005 industry Which activity in which country group achieved the greatest improvement in its labour productivity growth rate between 1975-1990 and 1990-2005?

options.A: agriculture in high-income countries
options.C: industry in East Asia

questions.questionText: The diagram, which shows part of the process that causes the aggregate demand curve to slope downwards to the right, is incomplete. rate of interest ......1...... level of aggregate price consumption level rises ......3...... real value of savings ......2...... Which words correctly complete gaps 1, 2 and 3?
The graph shows the rate of inflation in a country in a 5 year period. + rate of inflation 0
What might explain an increase in the volume of a country’s imports?

options.A: an appreciation of the country’s exchange rate
options.B: an increase in the country’s tariffs
options.C: a recession in the country
options.D: a rise in the country’s rate of income tax

questions.questionText: What is the most likely consequence of an increase in a country’s balance of payments deficit?

options.A: an increase in the foreign value of the currency of the country
options.B: an increase in the level of income within the country
options.C: a reduction in the quantity of money within the country
options.D: a reduction in unemployment within the country

questions.questionText: Which economic change might contribute to both cost-push and demand-pull inflation?

options.A: a fall in the exchange rate
options.B: a fall in the interest rate
options.C: a rise in the productivity of industrial workers
options.D: an improvement in the terms of trade

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the market for Japanese Yen. S S price of Yen in terms of other currencies D O quantity of Yen What could have caused the change in the supply of Yen from S to S ?

To reduce a deficit on the current account of the balance of payments, a government imposes a limit on the foreign exchange its people and firms can purchase. Why may this increase the country’s inflation rate?

options.A: Firms may have to purchase more expensive, domestically-produced raw materials.
options.B: Firms may have to sell more of their output on the domestic market.
options.C: The change in demand for foreign currency on the foreign exchange market may lead to an appreciation in the exchange rate.
options.D: The change in supply of the domestic currency on the foreign exchange market may reduce the money supply in the domestic economy.
